([[Fresno, California]]) | college = [[Stanford Cardinal men's basketball|Stanford]] (2006–2008) | draft_year = 2008 | draft_round = 1 | draft_pick = 10 | draft_team = [[Brooklyn Nets|New Jersey Nets]] | career_start = 2008 | career_end = | years1 = {{nbay|2008|start}}–{{nbay|2016|end}} | team1 = [[Brooklyn Nets|New Jersey / Brooklyn Nets]] | years2 = {{nbay|2017|full=y}} | team2 = [[Los Angeles Lakers]] | years3 = {{nbay|2018|start}}–{{nbay|2024|end}} | team3 = [[Milwaukee Bucks]] | years4 = {{nbay|2025|start}}–present | team4 = [[Los Angeles Clippers]] | highlights = * [[List of NBA champions|NBA champion]] ([[2021 NBA Finals|2021]]) * [[NBA All-Star]] ({{nasg|2013}}) * [[NBA All-Defensive Team|NBA All-Defensive First Team]] ({{nbay|2022|end}}) * [[NBA All-Defensive Team|NBA All-Defensive Second Team]] ({{nbay|2019|end}}) * [[NBA All-Rookie First Team]] ({{nbay|2008|end}}) * [[List of NBA Cup champions|NBA Cup champion]] ([[2024 NBA Cup|2024]]) * Third-team [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] – [[Associated Press|AP]], [[National Association of Basketball Coaches|NABC]] ([[2008 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|2008]]) * First-team [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Pac-10]] (2008) * Third-team [[Parade All-America Boys Basketball Team|''Parade'' All-American]] (2006) * [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-American]] ([[2006 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2006]]) | bbr = lopezbr01 }} '''Brook Robert Lopez''' (born April 1, 1988) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). Nicknamed "'''Splash Mountain'''", he was named an [[NBA All-Star]] as a member of the [[Brooklyn Nets]], and was voted twice to the [[NBA All-Defensive Team]] while with the [[Milwaukee Bucks]].{{Cite web |date=2019-05-16 |title=How Brook Lopez turned 'Splash Mountain' into a Bucks game-changer |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/26539884/how-brook-lopez-3-point-shooting-turned-splash-mountain-bucks-game-changer |access-date=2023-10-10 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}{{Cite web |date=2023-01-20 |title=Bucks' Brook Lopez Reacts to Disney's Splash Mountain News |url=https://wisportsheroics.com/brook-lopez-disneys-splash-mountain/ |access-date=2023-10-10 |language=en-us}} He won an [[NBA championship]] with Milwaukee in 2021. Lopez played two years of [[college basketball]] for the [[Stanford Cardinal men's basketball|Stanford Cardinal]]. He was selected as the 10th overall pick in the [[2008 NBA draft]] by the then-New Jersey Nets. He played for the Nets for nine seasons and is the [[List of National Basketball Association franchise career scoring leaders|franchise's all-time leading scorer]]. Lopez played one season with the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] before joining Milwaukee. His twin brother, [[Robin Lopez]], played in the NBA for 16 seasons. ==Early life== Lopez was born in [[Panorama City]], California (his family lived in Granada Hills at the time), to Deborah Ledford and his now deceased father, Heriberto Lopez, a native of [[Cuba]]. Lopez moved from Los Angeles to [[Oak Harbor, Washington]], while in second grade to be closer to his older brother, Alex, who was playing basketball at the [[Washington Huskies men's basketball|University of Washington]]. One year later, he moved to [[Fresno, California]], where he would spend the rest of his childhood and then attended [[San Joaquin Memorial High School]]. While at San Joaquin High School he played basketball with his twin brother, [[Robin Lopez]], and [[Quincy Pondexter]], both fellow future [[National Basketball Association|NBA]] players. As a 7 ft tall, 235 pound senior in high school, he averaged 13.6 points, 7.2 rebounds and 2.5 blocks. Both teammates played with Lopez on their successful [[AAU Men's Basketball All-Americans|AAU]] team, the Elite Basketball Organization (EBO), along with [[Derrick Jasper]] and Tre'Von Willis, both of [[UNLV Runnin' Rebels basketball|UNLV]]. Brook, along with his brother, Robin, committed to [[Stanford University]] early in 2005. Lopez's maternal grandfather played in the [[National Industrial Basketball League]] for the Milwaukee Allen-Bradleys.{{cite web |last1=Kuwada |first1=Robert |title=Lopez twins headed back to the family's basketball roots, and mom couldn't be happier |url=https://www.fresnobee.com/sports/article232635872.html |website=fresnobee |publisher=The Fresno Bee |access-date=November 28, 2022}} ==College career== [[Image:Robin and Brook Lopez.jpg|thumb|upright|left|Lopez (right) with his twin brother [[Robin Lopez|Robin]] in college]] The 2006–07 season was Lopez's first season at [[Stanford University]]. He was an [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Pac-10]] Honorable Mention and was named to the All-Pac-10 Freshman Team. He averaged 12.6 points and 6.0 rebounds over the course of his freshman season. The following season, he averaged 19.3 points, 8.2 rebounds, 1.5 assists and 2.1 blocks per game. In the second round of the [[2008 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2008 NCAA tournament]], Lopez hit the game-winning shot at the buzzer against the [[Marquette Golden Eagles men's basketball|Marquette Golden Eagles]] for an 82–81 overtime victory. He was named to the [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Pac-10 First Team]] and an [[2008 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American Third Team]] his [[2007–08 Stanford Cardinal men's basketball team|sophomore season]]. On March 31, 2008, both Lopez brothers declared for the [[2008 NBA draft]].{{cite web|title=Robin, Brook to enter NBA draft after two seasons at Stanford|date = March 31, 2008|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/draft2008/news/story?id=3322897|publisher=ESPN}} ==Professional career== ===New Jersey / Brooklyn Nets (2008–2017)=== ==== All-Rookie honors and increasing averages (2008–2011) ==== [[File:Brook Lopez.jpg|thumb|upright|Lopez with the [[New Jersey Nets]] in 2010]] Lopez was drafted by the [[Brooklyn Nets|New Jersey Nets]] 10th overall. His twin brother, Robin, was drafted 15th overall by the [[Phoenix Suns]]. Lopez played in his first NBA game on October 29, 2008, in a 95-85 Nets win. In his first game, Lopez came off the bench and had 8 points, 8 rebounds, and 2 blocks in 25 minutes.{{cite web|title=New Jersey Nets vs. Washington Wizards: NBA 2008-09 Season Opener|url=http://www.goldstar.com/events/washington-dc/new-jersey-nets-vs-washington-wizards-nba-2008-09-season-opener|work=Goldstar.com|publisher=goldstar}} Lopez began starting for the Nets after an injury took Josh Boone out of the line-up, and afterwards he started putting up solid numbers for the team. Lopez was selected to compete in the 2009 [[NBA All-Star Weekend Rookie Challenge]]. For his rookie season Lopez averaged 13.0 points, 8.1 rebounds and 1.9 blocks per game, playing in all 82 games of the regular season. He ranked 4th in the NBA in total blocks with 154 and 9th in blocks per game with 1.9, which was first among rookies.[https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/l/lopezbr01.html Brook Lopez] He finished third in the [[NBA Rookie of the Year]] voting and was named to the [[NBA All-Rookie Team|All-Rookie]] first team.{{cite web|title=Bulls' Rose takes home Rookie of Year Award|url=http://www.nba.com/2009/news/04/22/rose.roy.release/index.html|work=NBA.com|publisher=NBA|access-date=May 24, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090425041956/http://www.nba.com/2009/news/04/22/rose.roy.release/index.html|archive-date=April 25, 2009|url-status=dead}} He was selected as NBA Rookie of the Month twice in the months of January and February. The Nets finished at 34–48, failing to qualify for the playoffs. The Nets started the 2009–10 season going 0–18, the worst start to a season in NBA history. Because of their start the Nets fired head coach [[Lawrence Frank]].{{cite web|title=Nets fire Frank amid trip|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=4697789|work=[[ESPN]]|date = November 29, 2009|publisher=espn}} The Nets won their first game on December 4, 2009, against the [[Charlotte Bobcats]] 97–91. Lopez contributed in the win with 31 points and 14 rebounds.{{cite web|title=After 0-18 start, Nets break through for first win of season|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=291204017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161029174045/http://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=291204017|url-status=dead|archive-date=October 29, 2016|publisher=ESPN}} In his second season, Lopez established career bests in minutes played per game (36.9) and rebounds per game (8.6) while averaging 18.8 points per game. Lopez started in all the Nets' games in the 2009–10 season. Despite his improving play, however, the Nets struggled all season, finishing with one of the worst records in NBA history at 12–70; only 3 more wins than the 1972–73 [[Philadelphia 76ers]].{{cite web|title=Worst NBA Teams Ever|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/features/worstteams|publisher=ESPN}} For his third NBA season, Lopez for the third consecutive year played in all 82 regular season games. Lopez struggled to rebound the ball during the season and was criticized by head coach [[Avery Johnson]] because of his rebounding.{{cite news| url=http://articles.nydailynews.com/2010-12-04/sports/27083338_1_devin-harris-brook-lopez-overtime | archive-url=https://archive.today/20120707182633/http://articles.nydailynews.com/2010-12-04/sports/27083338_1_devin-harris-brook-lopez-overtime | url-status=dead | archive-date=July 7, 2012 | title=Avery blasts Brook as Nets falter again | location=New York | work=Daily News}} During the season the Nets traded for all-star point guard [[Deron Williams]]. The move helped Lopez out significantly, as he saw his scoring average increase. During the season Lopez averaged 20.4 points, 6.0 rebounds, 1.6 assists, and 1.5 blocks. The Nets finished at 24–58, once again missing the playoffs.{{cite web|title=New Jersey Nets: 2010–11 Season Review|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/671540-new-jersey-nets-2010-11-season-review|work=bleacherreport.com|publisher=bleacherreport}} ==== All-Star selection and injury-plagued seasons (2011–2014) ==== [[File:Brook Lopez against Bobcats.jpg|thumb|upright|Lopez with the [[Brooklyn Nets]] in 2013]] In the preseason of the lockout-shortened 2011–2012 campaign, Lopez broke his right foot and missed the first 32 games of the regular season. In his season debut against the [[Milwaukee Bucks]], Lopez finished with 9 points and 2 boards. In only his third game back, he scored a season-high 38 points in a road win over the [[Dallas Mavericks]]. Five games after his season debut, he injured his right ankle in a win over the [[Charlotte Bobcats]]. Due to the Nets' poor record, they decided to shut down Lopez for the remainder of the 2011–2012 season.{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/2012/news/04/06/nets-lopez.ap/index.html?ls=iref:nbahpt2 |title=Nets shut down C Brook Lopez for the season |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=April 7, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120409193355/http://www.nba.com/2012/news/04/06/nets-lopez.ap/index.html?ls=iref%3Anbahpt2 |archive-date=April 9, 2012 |url-status=dead }} In the little time that Lopez played he averaged 19.2 points and a career low in rebounds with 3.6. On July 11, 2012, the Nets re-signed Lopez to a four-year, $61 million contract extension.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/nets/news/Lopez_Signing_Release_120711.html|title=Brooklyn Nets Re-Sign Brook Lopez|work=NBA.com | date=July 11, 2012|access-date=July 12, 2012}} Lopez got off to a hot start in 2012, scoring 27 points in the season opener against the [[Toronto Raptors]]. He followed that performance by scoring 20 or more points in seven of the next twelve games, before injuring his ankle in a win over the [[Boston Celtics]] on November 28. The Nets struggled to a 2–5 record without Lopez before he returned on December 14. He began to play well again in late December, posting three straight 20 point, 10 rebound games, including a 35-point, 11 rebound performance in a win over the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] on December 29.{{cite news|title=Lopez pours in 35 as Nets clip Cavs|url=http://www.nypost.com/p/sports/nets/some_tall_tactics_3vTJYqBwlTNaFmQTeya7LK|work=nypost.com|publisher=nypost|first=Tim|last=Bontemps|date=December 30, 2012}} On January 30, 2013, NBA Commissioner [[David Stern]] selected Lopez to play in the [[2013 NBA All-Star Game]], his first All-Star appearance, replacing [[Rajon Rondo]] who had suffered a season-ending ACL injury.{{cite web|title=Brook Lopez Named To Eastern Conference All-Star Squad|date=January 30, 2013|url=http://newyork.cbslocal.com/2013/01/30/brook-lopez-named-to-eastern-conference-all-star-squad/|publisher=CBS News New York|access-date=January 30, 2013}} In the game, Lopez finished the game with 5 rebounds, 3 assists and 3 points in 11 minutes; all of his points came from the free throw line.{{cite news|last=Bontemps|first=Tim|title=Short All-Star night for Nets' Lopez|url=http://www.nypost.com/p/sports/more_sports/short_night_for_lopez_Fdk72CFBsuJISflG8oLN9K|work=nypost.com|publisher=nypost|access-date=February 19, 2013|date=February 18, 2013}} On March 20, 2013, the Nets were on the road playing the [[Dallas Mavericks]] when Lopez had 38 points and 11 rebounds in a 113-97 Nets win. His 38-point total was only 1 point away from his career high of 39.{{cite web |title= Brook Lopez-Deron Williams tandem powers Nets past Mavs |url= https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400278735 |publisher= [[ESPN]] |access-date= May 24, 2013}} At the end of the 2012–13 season, Lopez averaged 19.4 points and 6.9 rebounds, as he also set a new career high in blocks with 2.1. At the end of the season, the Nets won 49 games and were the fourth seed in the east.{{cite web |title= Brooklyn Nets end season with game vs. Detroit Pistons |url= http://www.netsdaily.com/2013/4/17/4233580/brooklyn-nets-end-season-with-game-vs-detroit-pistons |work= Netsdaily.com |date= April 17, 2013 |publisher= SBnation }} Lopez played all seven of the Nets playoff games, averaging 22.3 points and 7.4 rebounds. The Nets were eliminated in a seven-game, first-round series by the [[Chicago Bulls]]. In a season-opening loss at the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]], Lopez scored 21 points and grabbed 5 rebounds.{{cite news |title= New-look Nets fall to Cavaliers in opener as Deron Williams plays just 21 minutes |url= http://www.nydailynews.com/sports/basketball/nets/star-power-nets-brooklyn-season-opening-loss-cavs-article-1.1502188 |work= NYdailynews.com |publisher= NYdailynews |location= New York}} On November 15, 2013, Lopez logged 27 points and 7 rebounds in an [[overtime]] win over the [[Phoenix Suns]]. On December 7, 2013, Lopez had 32 points and 7 rebounds against the [[Milwaukee Bucks]].{{cite web |title= Brook Lopez, Nets bounce back to defeat Bucks |url= https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400489168 |publisher= ESPN}} On December 20, 2013, the Nets announced Lopez was out for the remainder of the season with a foot injury he had suffered the night before against the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].{{cite web|last=Youngmisuk|first=Ohm|title=Nets' Brook Lopez out for season|url=https://www.espn.com/new-york/nba/story/_/id/10175907/brooklyn-nets-lose-brook-lopez-season-broken-foot|website=[[ESPN]]|date=December 21, 2013}} In the 17 games that Lopez played, he averaged 20.7 points 6 rebounds, shot 56.3% from the field and 81.7% from the free throw line. This was the first season he didn't manage to record at least one [[double-double]].[https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/l/lopezbr01/gamelog/2014/ Brook Lopez 2013-14 Game Log] ==== 3-point improvement and franchise records (2014–2017) ==== On November 3, 2014, Lopez made his 2014–15 season debut after missing the first two games with a foot injury. In just under 24 minutes of action, he recorded 18 points, 6 rebounds, 2 blocks and 1 steal in the 116–85 win over the Oklahoma City Thunder.{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20141103/OKCBKN/gameinfo.html |title=Lopez returns as Nets rout injury-depleted Thunder |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=November 4, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160330124412/http://www.nba.com/games/20141103/OKCBKN/gameinfo.html |archive-date=March 30, 2016 |url-status=dead }} He went on to miss eight games between December 8 and 21 with a lower back strain, and following his return on December 23 against Denver, Lopez was benched in favor of [[Mason Plumlee]] who was the starting center in Lopez' absence. He remained coming off the bench for three more games before starting alongside Plumlee on December 30 against Chicago with [[Kevin Garnett]] out resting.[https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/l/lopezbr01/gamelog/2015/ Brook Lopez 2014-15 Game Log] He subsequently recorded 29 points, 5 rebounds and 2 blocks in the 96–82 win.{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20141230/BKNCHI/gameinfo.html |title=Lopez leads Nets over Bulls 96-82 |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=December 31, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160330124708/http://www.nba.com/games/20141230/BKNCHI/gameinfo.html |archive-date=March 30, 2016 |url-status=dead }} On March 20, 2015, Lopez recorded 32 points and a season-high 18 rebounds in a 129-127 triple overtime win over the Milwaukee Bucks.{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20150320/MILBKN/gameinfo.html |title=Lopez, Nets pull out 3-overtime victory over slumping Bucks |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=March 21, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170925084302/http://www.nba.com/games/20150320/MILBKN/gameinfo.html |archive-date=September 25, 2017 |url-status=dead }} On April 6, he was named the Eastern Conference Player of the Week for games played Monday, March 30 through Sunday, April 5. He led the Nets to a 3-1 week behind team-leading averages of 20.8 points (sixth in the conference), 10.3 rebounds (fourth in the conference) and 2.0 blocks (tied-fifth in the conference).{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/2015/news/04/06/brook-lopez-james-harden-players-of-the-week/index.html |title=Nets' Lopez, Harden named Players of the Week |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=April 6, 2015 June 26, 2015, Lopez opted out of his contract with the Nets to become a free agent.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/2015/news/06/26/brook-lopez-opts-out-of-contract-ap-report.ap/|title=Nets' Brook He moved past [[Richard Jefferson]] (8,507 points) into third place on the Nets' career scoring list.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160219/NYKBKN/gameinfo.html|title=Brook Lopez, Nets hand Knicks seventh straight loss, 109-98|work=NBA.com|date=February 19, 2016|access-date=February 19, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160219094832/http://www.nba.com/games/20160219/NYKBKN/gameinfo.html|archive-date=February 19, 2016|url-status=dead}} On March 24, with 22 points against the Cleveland Cavaliers, Lopez moved past [[Vince Carter]] into second place on the Nets' career scoring list with 8,835 points.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160324/CLEBKN/gameinfo.html|title=Nets blow by LeBron, Cavs in 4th, win 104-95|work=NBA.com|date=March 24, 2016|access-date=March 25, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160325091937/http://www.nba.com/games/20160324/CLEBKN/gameinfo.html|archive-date=March 25, 2016|url-status=dead}} During the offseason, Nets coach [[Kenny Atkinson]] told Lopez to be ready to become a [[three-point field goal|three-point shooting]] specialist during training camp.{{cite news |last=Stein |first=Mark |date=November 29, 2018 |title=Unwanted in L.A. Brook Lopez Became Milwaukee's 'Splash Mountain' |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2018/11/29/sports/basketball/brook-lopez-bucks.html |access-date=May 26, 2019 |newspaper=The New York Times}} On November 2, 2016, Lopez recorded 34 points and 11 rebounds in a 109–101 win over the [[Detroit Pistons]]. He hit four three-pointers during the game, matching his career total for three-pointers made;{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yzCLnOwJZbw |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211215/yzCLnOwJZbw |archive-date=2021-12-15 |url-status=live|title=Brook Lopez Matches Career Total with 4 Three Pointers!|work=YouTube.com|date=November 2, 2016|access-date=November 3, 2016}}{{cbignore}} he also made multiple three-pointers in a game for the first time in his career.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899507|title=Lopez double-double Leads Nets over Pistons|work=ESPN.com|date=November 2, 2016|access-date=November 3, 2016}} On November 15, he recorded 30 points, 10 rebounds and three blocks in a 125–118 loss to the [[Los Angeles Lakers]]. He became the Nets' franchise leader in blocked shots, passing [[George T.
